studies.title: When scoped Git change control is enough
studies.question: Does the governed workflow improve a known two-file repair over scoped Git change control with a capable reviewer?
studies.change: Use a fresh maintenance task spanning independent owners. Retain the simpler workflow if it produces the same authorized outcomes and recoverable history with less total review and recovery work.

claim.scope: The paired repair compares grant checks and observed file effects on a known two-file change.

studies.title: When a second receiver check changes closure
studies.question: When can an additional receiving-side read resolve a timeout after competent conventional status checking?
studies.change: Measure how often a separately operated projection remains fresh when ordinary status fails. Compare caller requests, total transport, time held and recovery effort before choosing where to place the second lookup.

claim.scope: The crossed study and its prospective follow-up test exact receiver status under prescribed schedules. They score verified effects separately from caller disposition and measure local lookup burden.

studies.title: Which scope earns a verifier rollout?
studies.question: Can a retained, evidence-bound qualification change safe rollout decisions or avoid repeated work?
studies.change: The local process check matched ordinary memoization. Test a separately operated consumer, including changes between lookup and relying on the result. Compare provenance, recovery and end-to-end cost under the same freshness requirement.

claim.scope: The replay tests scoped admission and fallback decisions for a synthetic verifier replacement.

studies.title: Did extracted routines help on later synthesis tasks?
studies.question: When does making previously discovered routines available improve verified synthesis on later task families under matched resource limits?
studies.change: Repeat the full scheduler and resource comparison on new task lineages with an independent task author and measured end-to-end cost. Change a reuse default only when the effect persists across the intended schedulers, budgets and tasks.

claim.scope: The synthetic studies test verified later task outcomes under fixed schedules, grammars and resource limits.

spotlight.label: Inspect the earlier retrieval miss in p01

runs.title: Grant revocation and delayed effect observation
runs.method: Replay a single local journal under ordered revocation, expiry and observation. Compare a cached permission, a version-checked transaction and a transaction carrying a serialized receipt.
runs.result_summary: The version-checked transaction and the serialized receipt agree on {schedules} schedules. An observation after revocation finds the valid earlier commit. Cached permission admits {unauthorized} unauthorized effects when the grant changes or expires before commit.
runs.limit: Ordered local fixture with a shared database and owner. Grant revision, commit tick and observation are distinct. The comparison leaves distributed control and production enforcement open.
runs.disposition: Check authority at the write, and use the effect journal to establish what committed.

runs.method: Replay four matched paths on separate disposable Git remotes. The conventional arm checks the grant against the proposed diff, tests the required configuration, and uses Git revert. Both arms receive the same known repair.
runs.result_summary: Both workflows accepted {accepted} authorized repairs in {pairs} matched paths. Both restored the remote file state. Scoped Git retained the original effect in ordinary branch ancestry and created {ordinary_files} additional receipt files. The governed arm retained it on an audit ref and created {governed_files} additional receipt files.
runs.limit: Retrospective replay of a known repair. Its approval is scripted. Receipt counts omit ordinary Git metadata and do not time human review.
runs.title: Four matched Git paths
runs.disposition: Keep scoped Git for the observed repair when its grant checks and recoverable branch history suffice.

runs.method: Cross every task with both deduplication contracts, four transport faults, and five observation profiles. The conventional arm checks exact current status and can retry against deduplication. The second arm adds a receiving-side read.
runs.result_summary: Conventional status closed {ordinary} of {pairs} matched cases. The added read closed {extra_route}. All {additional} extra closures occurred with stale or unavailable conventional status, a fresh second read, and no receiver deduplication. Both workflows closed {fresh} cases each when both observations were fresh.
runs.limit: Both reads use one simulated SQLite journal. The measured difference concerns evidence availability under logical time. Production isolation, incident frequency, and human effort are open. Its original safe-hold label used commit count without testing the identity of a lone committed effect. The separate effect-score run checks that distinction.
runs.title: Crossed receiver study
runs.disposition: Use ordinary status when it supplies a fresh exact observation. Add a read when its distinct availability settles a hold.

runs.method: Train two small text verifiers on authored cases. Give the conventional and retained-qualification workflows identical candidate results, approvals, monitors, fallback evidence and rules across seven observation profiles and two scopes.
runs.result_summary: Public-copy correctness rose from {prior_public} to {candidate_public} of {public_cases}. Protected record-change correctness fell from {prior_protected} to {candidate_protected} of {protected_cases}. Both workflows matched the authored decision at all {pairs} checkpoints. Post-hash document inspections went from {ordinary_reads} to {retained_reads}, with {writes} added writes.
runs.limit: Both workflows built and hashed the full evidence bundle before any cache check. The 140 and 80 counts describe subsequent inspections. The replay uses a relative regression rule and misses a shared error on copy-09. The follow-up adds a must-pass floor and conventional memoization.
runs.title: Paired verifier rollout
runs.disposition: Reuse a scoped decision where it saves enough work to pay for validity checks and writes. Compare equivalent conventional caching next.

runs.method: Compare no library, Jaccard retrieval of two historical programs, and two repeated adjacent routines extracted from earlier lineages. All arms use the same breadth-first enumerator, eight visible examples, a 96-proposal cap, and an independently implemented full-domain checker.
runs.result_summary: The no-library and extracted-routine arms each verified {basic} of {tasks} tasks. Ordinary retrieval verified {retrieval}. Retrieval exhausted its budget on {missed} case the other arms solved and solved {solved} they missed. All three exhausted their budgets on the {adverse} out-of-family cases. Retain ordinary retrieval for the next pilot at this scope.
runs.limit: Fixed, authored four-bit transformations with disjoint fixture identities, lineages and full target vectors. Search order, operator footprint, and lexical clues all matter. Candidate budgets match. The result preserves setup, proposal, screening and full-check costs. It supplies no evidence about scale or natural programs.
runs.title: Original four-bit pilot
runs.disposition: In the first corpus, keep whole-program retrieval as the tested benchmark. This run compares a query-aware whole-program arm with a query-blind routine arm.

runs.title: Selection × representation on five-bit maps
runs.method: Cross query-aware or query-blind selection with whole programs or extracted routines. Keep two library operators and a no-library arm. Use descriptive and neutral queries, two resource caps, four balanced orderings, and an independent exhaustive checker.
runs.result_summary: With the original handle-depth queue, descriptive queries and a proposal cap, query-aware whole programs verified {proposal_whole} of {stratum_cells} cells and routines verified {proposal_routine}. Under the expanded-work cap, the order reversed: {expanded_whole} for whole programs and {expanded_routine} for routines. All arms exhausted their budgets on the adverse family.
runs.limit: The 256 design cells reuse 16 authored five-bit tasks, so the cells are dependent. Cases and word size differ from the first pilot. Ordering changed some outcomes. Exhaustion does not establish impossibility, and the work cap excludes indexing and queue costs, which are reported separately. Primitive and library ordering were varied within this queue family. The separate scheduler run changes the queue priority itself.
runs.disposition: Retain whole-program retrieval as a comparator. In this follow-up, the routine-versus-whole ranking depends on the resource cap. Treat selection and representation as separate decisions, and keep the recommendation conditional on language cues and the full work budget.

runs.title: Disposition and observed effect
runs.method: Apply separate disposition and exact-effect scoring to the retained journal. Check committed operation, destination and payload against the locked task identity. Exercise seven controls before rescoring.
runs.result_summary: All {controls} controls passed, including a held case with one wrong effect. The stricter scorer changed {wrong_holds} historical hold labels. In the {pairs} retained pairs, conventional status still closed {ordinary} and the added read closed {extra}.
runs.limit: This rescores the same journal and retained local patch flag. The 160 pairs cross four authored task fixtures with forty conditions per task, so the closure counts describe this design. The wrong-effect case is an isolated instrument control. Both status paths use one simulated journal and clock. In a separate local check, an old failure with the current response tick causes a second commit without deduplication. A trusted source revision prevents that retry in the authored case.
runs.disposition: Carry disposition and observed effect as distinct fields. Treat a wrong or repeated effect as adverse even when the workflow holds.

runs.title: Matched access through one or two endpoints
runs.method: Cross primary and secondary projection freshness in separate local services. Compare primary-only status, a caller that can make a second request, and an ordinary gateway with the same access. Give every arm the same conditional retry rule and score the terminal journal separately.
runs.result_summary: Primary-only status verified {primary} of {pairs} paired cells. The two routes with second-projection access each verified {additional}. They agreed on disposition in all {agreement} cells. The gateway used {matched_calls} caller requests and {matched_bytes:,} status payload bytes. The additional endpoint used {additional_calls} caller requests and {additional_bytes:,} bytes.
runs.limit: The paired cells repeat four authored tasks. Status services run in separate processes under the same owner and receive controlled projections of the same starting operation journal. The protocol supplies trusted revision and known availability states. The comparison measures local IPC and logical observation costs. Separately administered outages, production time, incident frequency and human effort remain open.
runs.disposition: Use primary-only status where it supplies fresh exact evidence. A fresh second projection can close additional cases when primary status fails. Choose the caller or gateway placement by its full burden and failure behavior. In this run the gateway reduced caller requests and increased total status transport.

runs.title: Absolute floor and equal memoization
runs.method: Run the retained classifier outputs and scripted positive controls with a scoped must-pass rule. Compare a conventional memo with a serialized qualification over the same authoritative revision index. Test both missed updates and reviewers sharing one faulty dashboard.
runs.result_summary: The shared copy-09 failure routed to a specialist. Both workflows matched the expected route at {pairs} scripted checkpoints and each read {ordinary_reads} evidence documents. The serialized handoff wrote {handoff_bytes} bytes. Both caught a missed invalidation when the index next returned the current revision.
runs.limit: Eleven profiles each use two consumers and three logical ticks. The replay assumes unique case IDs, fixed reference labels and a current revision whenever the index responds. Separate intake controls found that the archived rule accepts a duplicate that masks a failure and a changed label that matches a wrong prediction. The index can fail to respond in these profiles. This run did not include a successful stale response. One local follow-up checks exact revision matching with a trusted revision in the request. A second obtains that revision from a separate same-owner process and counts pipe payload. Independent operation and production fault isolation remain open. CPU timings are diagnostic.
runs.disposition: Use ordinary memoization at the tested boundary. Before routing on submitted predictions, check the complete set of case IDs and labels against a separately controlled reference. Require evidence of freshness and hold when it cannot be established.

runs.title: Scheduler sensitivity at matched caps
runs.method: Replay every retained five-bit arm, then change only the queue priority from handle depth to expanded primitive length. Use the same inputs, libraries, verifier, order conditions, and two resource caps.
runs.result_summary: In {stratum} descriptive-query cells at the proposal cap, prioritizing expanded length changed query-aware whole programs from {whole_prior} to {whole_reordered} verified cells. Query-aware routines verified {routines_prior} and {routines_reordered}. The earlier ranking depended on the scheduler as well as the cap.
runs.limit: The {pairs} matched cells repeat conditions over sixteen authored tasks. Counts describe cells in this design. Treat task lineage as the unit for inference about new tasks. The read-only audit observed the focal pattern before this pinned rerun, so the result is exploratory for unseen families.
runs.disposition: Keep both representations and prespecify schedule, budget, and outcome denominators. Choose a representation only after the advantage persists across comparable schedulers on independent tasks.

agenda.question: Does independently available receiver status settle outcomes ordinary status cannot?
agenda.rival: The earlier benefit reflects access to fresh information. One conventional endpoint with the same access ought to suffice.
agenda.test: At the same fault and retry budget, compare one conventional status endpoint with a workflow that adds a separately operated reader. Give the single-endpoint baseline all evidence it could ordinarily obtain. Cross receiver deduplication with shared and separate upstream failures. Record verified and false closures, wrong and repeated effects, time to resolution and operating cost.
agenda.decisions: Keep a separate read only where it adds verified closures with acceptable cost and no repeated effects. Adopt one channel on parity. Narrow the architecture claim if the extra path makes holds or duplicates worse.

agenda.question: When does a serialized qualification help across a real consumer boundary?
agenda.rival: The current equal-memoization replay already matches work and decisions. A transportable record matters only where consumers cannot share one in-process memo and still enforce freshness.
agenda.test: The local process check gave both arms the same revision authority and pipe traffic. Next compare independently operated consumers with the same freshness bound. Vary delayed notification, no response, successful stale responses, and an update concurrent with use. Charge for freshness, evidence access, encoding, exchange, and recovery.
agenda.decisions: Keep ordinary memoization when it meets the contract. Admit a handoff only for a consumer with a measured benefit under the same stale-read and expiry conditions. Hold when freshness or regression evidence cannot be verified.

agenda.question: Does the measured reuse advantage survive independently authored tasks and different schedulers?
agenda.rival: Counting archived routines as one handle moves whole programs earlier in one queue, even when they expand to more work. Descriptive cues and the task family may also drive the result.
agenda.test: Use independent task authors and compare both representations and query policies at matched library size, scheduler and time budget. Freeze resource caps and the full-cost accounting before opening outcomes.
agenda.decisions: Choose a representation only where an advantage persists for the intended schedule and resource cap. Keep both comparators where the ranking changes. Record exhaustion, regressions and costs.
